 Order

This revision is filed by the revision petitioner / accused No.1 under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the CR.P.C.' for short) challenging the order dated 19.11.2014 in C.C.No.720/2011 on the file of JMFC (III Court), Mysore whereby the learned Magistrate has dismissed the application filed by the accused for discharge under Section 239 of Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.1 as well as learned High Court Government Pleader.
Perused the records.
3. The complainant / respondent No.1 filed a private complaint against the accused for the offence under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The learned Magistrate has NC: 2023:KHC:33823 referred the matter under Section 156 of Cr.P.C. to the jurisdictional Police and the Investigating Officer after investigation submitted the charge sheet for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
The accused after appearance filed application under Section 239 for discharge and the same was rejected by the learned Magistrate.
This order is being challenged.
4. The revision petitioner is accused No.1 before the trial Court.
According to the prosecution, the accused No.1 acquired right, title and interest in respect of the house property bearing door No.523 situated in II Ramachandra, Agrahara, Mysore.
It is also alleged that he agreed to sell the suit schedule property for a consideration of Rs.4,75,000/- to the complainant and on 19.03.1999, a registered sale deed was executed.
It is also alleged that the accused has made the complainant to believe that the property was free from all encumbrance and he has also shown certain documents to believe the said aspect.

According to the prosecution, thereafter, the complainant has invested huge amount in the said property so as to make it fit for human dwelling and he was enjoying the property by getting khatha changed in his NC: 2023:KHC:33823 name.

It is also alleged that suddenly he received a notice from State Bank of Mysore invoicing the sale of immovable properties and the property of the complainant, which he has purchased from accused was shown to be at Sl.No.523.
It is alleged that the loan was availed by accused No.2 and accused Nos.1 and 3 were the guarantors.
Hence, a complaint came to be lodged.

sentences.text:
The main contention of the learned counsel for the revision petitioner is that in 2001, O.A.
proceedings were initiated wherein the present complainant was a party but the allegations were in respect of the sale in 1999 making allegation that the property is free from all encumbrance.

Subsequent to impleading of the complainant in the civil litigation does not discharge the burden of the accused as there is a specific allegation that the property was alleged to have been free from all encumbrances, but it was sold by cheating to the complainant and they received the entire sale consideration under the false pretext.

It is asserted that the complaint was filed in the year 2011, but delay and other things cannot be considered at the juncture as there are certain allegations regarding receipt of the notice etc. and all those matters are NC: 2023:KHC:33823 required to be tested only during the course of the trial.

Though the matter is pending since, 2015, all along, no initiation was taken to argue the matter and now it is argued that the revision petitioner / accused is a senior citizen, but that itself is not a ground.
The other two accused have not challenged the order of framing the charge.
The remedy for the revision petitioner is to face the trial and to prove his innocence.
What is required to be proved in the trial cannot be considered at this juncture during the discharge application.
The learned Magistrate has appreciated all these aspects in its proper perspective and has rightly dismissed the application under Section 239 of Cr.P.C filed by the revision petitioner/accused.
No illegality or perversity is found in the said order and the said order does not suffer from any infirmity.
Hence, the revision petition being devoid of any merit does not survive for consideration and needs to be rejected.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The revision petition stands dismissed.

(ii) Send back the entire TCRs to the trial Court along with copy of this order with a direction to NC: 2023:KHC:33823 proceed with the trial in expeditious manner and dispose of the matter at the earliest.
